title: Pre-Sorted Tsetlin Machine (The Genetic K-Medoid Method)
new_feature: A pre-sort stage before TM training: a genetic algorithm solves Hamming-distance maximum dispersion to seed binary K-medoid clustering per class, then a genetic algorithm aligns clusters across classes to maximise inter-class Hamming distance, and each aligned group trains its own smaller TM.

extraction_notes: Dataset sizes not stated; 80/20 random splits of each dataset (unclear whether official train/test were pooled). EMNIST split unspecified. Table values are 'critical datapoints' whose K (number of medoids) is not stated. Caveat: pre-sorted TMs used early stopping when accuracy reached 100% via inference between epochs, apparently on the evaluation data, and training time counts the fastest of two strategies; at inference it is not described how a test point is routed to its cluster TM, so reported accuracies may be optimistic. Per-K curves only in Figs. 10-12 (not extracted).
caution: Training stopped once accuracy reached 100%, apparently measured on the evaluation data, and test-time routing to a cluster TM is not described: accuracies are likely optimistic.
